model.name: Data Catalog Entry / Data Product
model.purpose: Represent one governed catalog record and the distinct data-product offering it describes so agents can discover, evaluate and request consumption without confusing metadata publication with resource availability, authorization, delivery, fitness or use.
model.scope_statement: Owns catalog-record identity, version and lifecycle; separate offering identity and product semantics; discovery and classification; purpose, value and intended use; roles; dataset, service, distribution, contract, schema, lineage and quality references; interface and access-route descriptions; rights, privacy, commercial and service-term references; quality and SLO summaries; feedback, usage indicators, provenance, lifecycle, federation, correction, access, retention, audit and projections. Dataset bytes, services, distributions, policies, agreements, subscriptions, orders, deliveries, usage events, issues, audits and records masters remain external where authoritative.
in_scope: Catalog record and distinct data-product offering identity, ownership, purpose, discovery, classifications, coverage, versions and provenance
Non-owning resource composition, interfaces, access routes, rights and terms, quality and SLO summaries, feedback, lifecycle, federation, records and projections
out_of_scope: Owning Dataset, Data Service, Distribution, Contract, Schema, Lineage, Quality Assessment, Policy, Agreement, Subscription, Order, Delivery, Usage, Issue, Audit or Records masters
Treating listing or publication as proof of discoverability, availability, authorization, delivery, acceptance, fitness or usage

Autonomous resource publication, access approval, licence or contract change, subscription, payment, delivery, dataset mutation, quality certification, service retirement or physical records disposition

boundary_notes.distinction: The candidate relation identifies governed data resources and versions. The catalog record and offering own discovery and product context but not dataset identity, bytes or lifecycle.

boundary_notes.neighbor: CatalogRecord, DataProduct, DatasetSeries, Distribution and DataService
boundary_notes.distinction: These identities remain separate. One record describes one resource head; an offering composes resources by role without collapsing them.

boundary_notes.neighbor: WM-DAT-004 Data Schema / Data Contract, WM-DAT-006 Data Lineage and WM-DAT-007 Data Quality Assessment
boundary_notes.distinction: The catalog stores versioned references and qualified summaries but not authoritative contract, schema, lineage or assessment lifecycles.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Policy, agreement, subscription, order, delivery, usage, issue, audit and records
boundary_notes.distinction: These masters retain independent parties, authority, state, evidence and time. The catalog describes routes and references but executes none of them.

boundary_notes.neighbor: DCAT, DCAT-AP, DPROD, ODPS, Schema.org, DataCite, FAIR, PROV, DQV, ODRL, DPV, OpenAPI and time
boundary_notes.distinction: Each source has a distinct scope and normative force. Every mapping is version-pinned, profile-qualified and loss-declaring.

sources.title: Open Data Product Specification

sources.title: Dataset

sources.relevance: Frames research-data lifecycle, stakeholders, governance and reuse.

sources.title: FAIR Guiding Principles for scientific data management and stewardship

sources.title: Time Ontology in OWL

sources.relevance: Defines timestamps with seconds and explicit UTC relationship.

sources.relevance: Defines HTTP API interface descriptions, operations, schemas, responses and security schemes.

composition.target: DCAT 3, DCAT-AP 3.0.1, DPROD 1.0 Beta 1, ODPS 4.1, Schema.org Dataset, DataCite 4.6, FAIR, PROV-O, DQV, ODRL 2.2, DPV 2.0, OpenAPI 3.1.1, OWL-Time and RFC 3339
composition.purpose: Project version-pinned discovery, product, citation, provenance, quality, rights, privacy, interface and time views with declared loss.

owner_package_requirements: Dimension owner, namespace authority, catalog governance mandate and accountable data product owner

Authoritative Catalog Record, Data Product, Dataset, Data Service, Distribution, Contract, Schema, Lineage, Quality, Policy, Agreement, Subscription, Delivery, Usage, Issue, Audit and Records registries
Approved discovery, taxonomy, access, licence, privacy, quality, service-level, publication, federation, retention and interoperability profiles
Role, delegation, review, exception, correction, deprecation, withdrawal and agent-operation policies
dimension.namespace_guidance: Mint catalog-record, record-version, offering, product-version, composition, route, term-profile, feedback, correction and projection IDs; preserve every external master identifier.

canonicalization_rules: Canonicalize a catalog record by authoritative record identifier and catalog namespace; canonicalize the offering separately by authoritative product identifier and owner namespace.
Keep CatalogRecord, DataProduct or offering, Dataset, DatasetSeries, Distribution, DataService, Policy, Agreement, Subscription, Delivery and Usage identities separate.
patch_rules: Extensions declare product type, domain, resource roles, vocabulary, access, rights, privacy, quality, SLO, lifecycle, records and interoperability effects.
Published record versions are immutable; changes create linked successors with reason, impact and review.
Never silently change offering identity, owner, resource version, purpose, interface, access route, rights, price, contract, SLO, quality claim, lifecycle state or evidence.
compatibility_rules: Ignore additive fields only when record and offering identity, resource bindings, owner, purpose, authority, time, access, rights, quality and provenance survive.
Every projection pins standard, vocabulary, schema and mapping versions and declares information loss.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier for each catalog record, offering, resource binding, policy reference or artifact, qualified by issuer, namespace and record kind.
Governed globally resolvable catalog-record or offering IRI.
Dimension UUID or ULID when neither preceding identifier exists.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Use RFC 3339 timestamps with seconds and explicit offset or Z; distinguish product, resource, event, effective, publication, modification, deprecation, withdrawal, recorded, ingestion and knowledge times whenever they differ.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Store digest, media type, record kind, offering and resource scope, profile versions, actor, event and knowledge times, confidentiality marking and provenance.

policies: The catalog owns registration records, discovery descriptions, composition references and version lineage but not Dataset, Data Service, Distribution, Contract, Policy, Agreement, Subscription, Delivery, Usage, Issue, Audit or Records masters.
Listing, discoverability, availability, authorization, delivery, acceptance, fitness and usage are independent assertions with separate sources, authority, evidence and time.
A product description may persist when resources are unavailable or withdrawn, subject to records and privacy policy.

Agents cannot autonomously publish resources, approve access, change licences or contracts, create subscriptions or payments, perform delivery, mutate datasets, certify quality, retire services or dispose records without delegated authority.

read: Resolve record and offering heads, owner, purpose, classifications, resources, interfaces, access, rights, terms, quality, SLO, feedback, provenance, lifecycle, federation and projection loss under the permitted view.
create: Bind stable record and offering identities, catalog, owner, purpose, audience, authoritative resource references, source, authority and initial lifecycle before publication.
update: Append successor descriptions, bindings, profiles, observations, reviews, exceptions, corrections and lifecycle assertions with reason, authority, expected revision, event time and knowledge time.
delete: Apply legal hold, citation persistence, privacy, security and adopting-Dimension records policy; withdraw or tombstone only the catalog view without cascading to product, resource, policy, agreement, usage or records masters, and let authoritative systems execute physical disposition.

roles.name: Catalog authority
responsibilities: Own catalog scope, registration rules, publication policy, federation and record lifecycle.

roles.name: Data product owner
responsibilities: Own offering purpose, value, resource composition, consumer outcomes and accountable use.

roles.name: Data steward
responsibilities: Own dataset semantics, taxonomy, quality, provenance and authoritative metadata bindings.

roles.name: Service and distribution owner
responsibilities: Own endpoints, formats, operations, delivery routes, SLOs and support evidence.

roles.name: Rights, privacy and access authority
responsibilities: Own licence, policy, purpose, eligibility, privacy, agreement and access-decision references.

roles.name: Catalog curator and reviewer
responsibilities: Review descriptions, classifications, versions, evidence, conflicts, limitations and lifecycle proposals.

roles.name: Records and federation steward
responsibilities: Own harvesting, conflict, correction, retention, tombstone, audit and projection policy.

access.default_rule: Deny personal or sensitive metadata, credentials, protected endpoints, commercial terms, consumer identities, usage details, unpublished evidence and internal issues unless a purpose-bound policy permits the minimum necessary view.
exceptions: Declared operational, safety, incident, privacy, legal, audit or subject-rights access must cite authority, scope, purpose and time limit and must be logged.
audit_requirements: Log actor, agent, role, purpose, catalog record and version, offering, operation, authority, policy, RFC 3339 time, affected references, source revision and outcome without unnecessary protected-data duplication.

read_order: Read Dimension catalog governance, namespace, product, dataset, service, contract, quality, rights, privacy, access, federation, retention and agent policies.

Read this catalog record and linked product, dataset, service, distribution, contract, schema, lineage, quality, policy, agreement, subscription, delivery, usage, issue, audit and records models before mutation.

coverage.claim: WM-DAT-008 covers one governed catalog record and its distinct data-product offering from identity, purpose and composition through discovery, coverage, interfaces, access routes, rights, terms, quality, SLOs, feedback, lifecycle, federation, records and projections. Domain profiles, changing beta or current-at-access specifications and independent external review remain deferred.

known_omissions: Claude and Grok each timed out on one bounded attempt; no independent external result was admitted.
The WM-DAT-001 relation remains candidate and grants no approved ownership or cascade behavior.
DPROD 1.0 Beta 1 and current-at-access profiles require future version review and conformance testing.
Domain taxonomies, commercial terms, legal rules, access workflows, quality methods and service-level calculations require separate profiles.
conflicts: CatalogRecord, DataProduct or offering, Dataset, DatasetSeries, Distribution, DataService, Policy, Agreement, Subscription, Delivery and Usage are not interchangeable identities.
Listed, discoverable, available, authorized, delivered, accepted, fit and used require distinct states.
Unknown, unavailable, not applicable, confidential, withheld, deprecated, withdrawn, retired and deleted require distinct states.
regional_assumptions: Rights, privacy, contracting, pricing, access, retention and publication authority depend on jurisdiction and organization.
DCAT-AP is a European profile; DPROD is beta; ODPS, Schema.org, DataCite, FAIR, DPV and OpenAPI are scoped profiles, not universal operating law.
adversarial_checks: Reject a record that collapses catalog identity, offering identity and resource identity.
Reject a product without stable identity, owner, purpose, authoritative resource bindings, source, lifecycle and current head.
Reject inference from listing to availability, authorization, delivery, acceptance, fitness or use.
Reject autonomous resource publication, access approval, agreement change, subscription, payment, delivery, dataset mutation, quality certification, service retirement or disposition.
Reject a projection that omits release pins, mapping provenance, conflict handling or information-loss declarations.
